subject: Next steps: feature-parity evaluation (tool-calling, structured outputs, streaming)

Subject: Next steps: feature-parity evaluation (tool-calling, structured outputs, streaming)

Hi Priya / Rajiv — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + proposed next steps so the eval stays tightly scoped: 

Summary of what we heard (please correct if I missed anything):
- Primary use-case: conversational assistant that issues tool/function calls to internal services (lookup, order status, billing queries) and returns validated structured outputs to downstream systems.
- Streaming requirement: live user-facing transcripts and progressive partial responses for faster perceived latency.
- Throughput & SLOs: ~300 concurrent requests during peak, target p50 latency <= 200ms for short responses, tail latency tolerances for long-running tool calls.
- Constraints: hard data-residency requirement (US), KMS-managed keys, and a cost target that keeps per-conversation token spend predictable.

Competitive context we want to validate in the POC:
1) Tool/function calling parity: can we reliably invoke external functions (and surface structured results) with the same semantics your engineers currently get from HyperscalerX? We want to test: 1) invocation reliability under 50 concurrent calls, 2) error propagation / retries, 3) traceability to call IDs.
2) Structured outputs: enforceable JSON schema validation with deterministic failure modes (when model diverges).
3) Streaming: progressive tokens + ability to pipe partial outputs to your UI without re-assembling afterwards.

Proposed next steps (timeline + owners):
- Redwood provides an evaluation plan + test harness (streams + function stubs) — Hannah & Neha — by 2026-05-06 (attached: redwood-feature-parity-plan.pdf).
- FastMedia provides a small representative dataset + sample function endpoints (or allow Redwood to hit stubs in our test sandbox) — Priya/Rajiv — by 2026-05-08.
- Kickoff POC run (2 weeks): functional parity tests + performance runs comparing Redwood hosted endpoints vs Hyperscaler baseline (we can also run against a Private deployment if you prefer) — target start 2026-05-10.
- Deliverables: pass/fail matrices for each test, perf numbers (p50/p95/p99), example traces, recommended configuration (batching, quantization profile) and a short cost projection for your projected 2M tokens/mo usage.

Open questions we flagged on the call:
- Do you want the POC run against Hosted Redwood API or the Private VPC image?
- Any strict lockdowns on external test endpoints we should know about (IP allowlists, egress rules)?


Cost estimate note: I’ll give a preliminary cost range in the next email after I confirm the exact test mix (streaming vs non-streaming tokens).

Attached to this message: redwood-feature-parity-plan.pdf (high-level test matrix) and a small sample harness we’ll share in the repo if you want to review.

If that plan looks good, can we lock 2026-05-10 for a 60-minute kickoff? I’ll include Neha (SE) for the technical runbook and Marissa for post-POC adoption/next-step coordination.

Thanks — Hannah

1) Data residency & KMS: we are required to keep customer PII in-region (US) and we need Redwood to integrate with our AWS KMS keys. Is that supported in Hosted mode, or do we need Private?
2) Cost: our rough projection is ~2M generated tokens / month. Can you give a high-level delta vs the Hyperscaler baseline? We don’t need exacts yet, just ballpark so finance can pencil in numbers.
3) Test environment: for the initial parity checks, is it ok if you run against Redwood Hosted endpoints, or do you recommend Private from day one? Our security team will probably prefer a VPC approach but would like to avoid extra ops unless necessary.

We can get you a small dataset and function stubs by 2026-05-08. 2026-05-10 looks fine for kickoff — propose 10:00 AM PT.

Subject: Re: Next steps: feature-parity evaluation (tool-calling, structured outputs, streaming)

Hi Priya — quick answers inline and a proposed concrete plan: 

1) Data residency & KMS: Redwood Hosted supports customer KMS integrations (AWS KMS) for encryption-at-rest and has regional deployments in US-only regions. For the tightest isolation we can run Redwood Private (VPC) — both are options. If you want us to use your AWS KMS keys in Hosted we can do that under a controlled config; I’ll loop in our compliance lead if we move forward.

2) Cost, ballpark: for a mixed workload (streaming + structured outputs) our Hosted estimate ballparks at ~$0.0010 per generated token equivalent (this is a rough starting point; the POC will refine). For 2M tokens/month that maps to ~$2,000/mo before any reserved-capacity discounts. Hyperscaler baseline (what you referenced) tends to be ~1.2–1.5x higher for similar latency SLAs — we’ll put a formal comparison in the POC report.

3) Test environment recommendation: start Hosted for speed (no infra ops), run the parity tests and perf runs. If results look good and security wants Private, we can stage a Private onboarding for staging.

What we’ll deliver before kickoff (Hannah / Neha):
- A small preconfigured test harness repo (includes redwood-eval-script-sample.py) — will share link by EOD 2026-05-06.
- A short runbook for streaming and tool-calling tests (how we measure and the pass/fail criteria).
- A sandbox endpoint you can use to point your function stubs at (IP allowlist support).

Action items: 
- Priya/Rajiv: confirm if Hosted is acceptable for initial POC or if we must start Private. (reply by 2026-05-07)
- FastMedia: share dataset + stubs by 2026-05-08.
- Redwood: share test harness + kickoff agenda by 2026-05-06.

Attaching a small sample script (redwood-eval-script-sample.py) showing streaming + function-calling snippets and wiring for schema validation. I’ll also drop a Drive link with a fuller test matrix.

Thanks — looking forward.

Hannah
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
